clue.text: Calamity resulting from Diana's bloomer

parts.note: DI is the short form of the name Diana, with the possessive S kept
a bloomer is something that blooms, here a flower, the aster

explanation.surface: A botched effort by someone called Diana has gone badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, which fits the calamity, but it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a terrible misfortune, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Condescend to take on board son's plan

indicators.note: taking something on board means holding it inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: to deign is to condescend
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to accept a son's scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or intention, a synonym of plan.

clue.text: Things of no importance in glass?

definitions.text: Things of no importance in glass?

parts.words: Things of no importance in glass?
parts.note: the idiom for trivial matters, read literally as a weak ale served in a pint pot

explanation.surface: Trivial bits and pieces found in a drinking vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means trivia; literally it is a weak, low-alcohol ale, which is what might sit in a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes unimportant matters, and literally names a weak brew poured into a tumbler.

clue.text: After fuss, difficult dismissing hotel's sommelier, perhaps

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first in this down entry

parts.note: to be in a stew is to be in a fuss

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: hard means difficult
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: After a commotion, a tricky wine waiter is sacked from the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' takes the H out of HARD, leaving ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine waiter is one kind of attendant who serves passengers or diners, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Level prior to tense incident

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so the first piece precedes the letter

parts.note: even means level
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Things were calm before a tense episode.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence or happening, a synonym of incident.

clue.text: Quietly, the man occupies young relative

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: young things are new
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
the man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: A man quietly moves in with a youthful relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young relative' reads as one phrase, but 'young' is wordplay and 'relative' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family member, a kind of relation.

clue.text: No longer active, former leader of Conservatives put in shade

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the initial goes within the colour

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An ex-Tory leader has been eclipsed and is no longer active.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of Conservatives' reads as a politician, but it is just the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that will never erupt again is dead, no longer in action.

clue.text: Any he shot brings scavenger

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Any man who fires a gun will bring a scavenging animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This African carnivore is famous for feeding on carrion, so it is a scavenger.

clue.text: Absented oneself and sketched

parts.note: with can mean and, as in bread with butter
drew means sketched

explanation.surface: Someone left the room and did some drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a mere link but gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave or pull out from a gathering is to absent oneself from it.

clue.text: Made sense of Fahrenheit in Germany

parts.note: in as in staying in, being at home
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Someone understood the Fahrenheit scale while in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but gives letters meaning not out.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to the bottom of something is to understand it, to comprehend.

clue.text: Bulletin about split in Foggy Bottom

indicators.note: about means going around, so the one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a bulletin is an official statement
to split is slang for to leave, depart

explanation.surface: A news bulletin reports a division in some misty low-lying place.
explanation.walkthrough: Foggy Bottom is the Washington DC district housing the US foreign ministry, and its nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The American foreign affairs ministry is headquartered in Foggy Bottom, so the place name stands for it by metonymy.

clue.text: Brave face social worker put on

indicators.note: put on means added after, so the insect follows the cheek in this across entry

parts.note: face as in nerve or cheek, which is gall
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A care worker bravely puts on a front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare officer; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant means bold and courageous, a synonym of brave.

clue.text: Answer's to be found in proven and reliable political publication

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: hard facts are proven and reliable ones
ANS is a standard abbreviation of answer; the apostrophe S reads as is

explanation.surface: A reply turns up in some trustworthy political record.
explanation.walkthrough: Hansard is the official verbatim record of debates in the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed transcript of parliamentary debates is a publication about politics.

clue.text: Swinger having choice about dancing nude

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fruit goes round the other letters

parts.note: a plum job is a choice one

indicators.note: dancing letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A swinger with a choice of naked dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' is the anagram signal for 'nude'; 'Swinger' suggests a partygoer, but it means something hanging that swings, like a clock weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight on a clock that moves to and fro is something that swings.

clue.text: Member, before holiday, gets delivery

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second in this down entry

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: An MP gets a parcel before going on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a leg-break is a spin ball bowled to turn from leg to off; a ball bowled is called a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a spun ball is one kind of ball bowled, and each bowled ball is called a delivery.

clue.text: Culinary herb helping to make healthy meal

indicators.note: helping to make says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A kitchen herb helps produce a wholesome dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant plant used for seasoning food is a cooking herb.

clue.text: Tuna in foil, newly prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fish cooked in foil, freshly made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' looks like it modifies 'prepared' but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a species of large ocean fish, an example of tuna.

clue.text: Nothing left in safe?

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: if everything is on the right side, nothing is on the left
safe means unharmed or okay; the question mark flags the cryptic first reading

explanation.surface: Someone checks the strongbox and finds it empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an empty safe; 'safe' is the definition, and 'Nothing left' is a playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurt and okay mean safe and well, the everyday sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Large curved structure in wood

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an arch is a curved structure spanning an opening

explanation.surface: A big arched construction stands in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber of this deciduous conifer is a type of wood.

clue.text: Powerful chief, fiery type

parts.note: hot as in strong, powerful, like hot spice
the head is the chief

explanation.surface: A mighty boss is someone with a fiery temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: An impetuous, quick-tempered person is a fiery character.

clue.text: Idol with magic formula in musical

parts.note: an idol is a god that is worshipped
a spell is a magic formula of words

explanation.surface: A worshipped figure with an enchantment appears in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Godspell is a 1971 stage musical based on the Gospel of Matthew.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known stage show with songs, so it is an example of a musical.

clue.text: Baseball player, parking it, caught that woman

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a woman referred to is her

explanation.surface: A baseball player parking a car is caught by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The player who throws the ball to the batter in baseball is a member of the fielding team.

clue.text: Make fun of star's second service

parts.note: to tease is to make fun of

indicators.note: second means the second letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Mocking a celebrity's second appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests duty; here it is a matching collection of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cups, saucers and pot is called a service, as in dinner service.

clue.text: List must include ordinary farmyard bird

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so the letter goes within the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty

explanation.surface: A list must include an everyday bird from the farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is the male chicken that crows in a farmyard.

clue.text: Elated, being broadcast

definitions.meaning: to be walking ... is to be elated
a programme going out live is transmitting, being broadcast

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is short for the idiom 'walking on air'.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmitting live on radio or television and feeling overjoyed both fit the phrase.

clue.text: Explore underground pool, with most of them swimming

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely into a new order
most of a word is all but its final letter

explanation.surface: An underground pool where most people go swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the M from 'them' to leave THE; 'swimming' mixes POOL and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go caving is to explore caves and shafts below ground, a verb sense.

clue.text: Cycle ultimately crashed entering ring

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the letter goes within the bells

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cyclist finally crashed into a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to ride a bicycle, so cycle is a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Significant changes covering court's antisocial work periods

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the outer words enclose the courtyard

parts.note: grave means serious, significant
shifts are changes
a yard is a court, as in courtyard

explanation.surface: Major changes in a court's working hours that are unsociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' means the two outer words wrap round the court; 'court' is a yard, as in courtyard, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight stints of labour are worked at hours that disrupt normal social life.

clue.text: Stream of abuse from one stuck in traffic

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside, so the numeral goes within the other word

parts.note: traffic as a verb or noun means trade, buying and selling
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in traffic lets out a volley of curses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like road jams; here it means commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech of denunciation is an outpouring of insults.

clue.text: Absurd article describing new instrument

indicators.note: describing in crosswords means drawing round, so the letters go around the abbreviation
absurd suggests the letters are made nonsense of and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ridiculous item describing a newly made instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absurd' rearranges ARTICLE into CLARIET, which goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woodwind with a single reed, an example of a musical instrument.
